capture_engagement.description: Whether the engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) of the email are captured as analytics events of the recipient. Defaults to true. A project whose admin turned engagement capture off captures nothing, whatever the send says. A send with `template_id` takes it only in the beta for sending email from code.

distinct_id.description: Distinct ID of the recipient's person. The send and its engagement events are recorded against that person. Defaults to the recipient's email address.

from.description: Sender of the email, as `security@example.com` or `Example <security@example.com>`, on a verified domain of the project. Without it, an email your code rendered goes out from the project's default sender, or from its only verified sender when it has no default, and an uploaded template from its own sender. A send with `template_id` doesn't take it.

html.description: HTML body of the email, exactly as the recipient should see it. Through this tool the whole request as JSON, html and text included, must stay under 1 MiB, and quotes and line breaks count twice. A larger email can't be sent here.

reply_to.description: Addresses replies to the email go to. A send with `template_id` doesn't take it.

subject.description: Subject of the email your code rendered.

template_key.description: Key that names the email, such as welcome, so its metrics, logs and status group under it. Letters, numbers, hyphens (-) and underscores (_) only.

text.description: Plain text body of the email. Without it, PostHog derives the text from html. Through this tool the whole request as JSON, html and text included, must stay under 1 MiB.
